Bug_Details:
This call doesn't make sense. For any collection c, calling c.containsAll(c) should
always be true, and c.retainAll(c) should have no effect.
     c c.containsAll(c) c.retainAll(c)
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by including two vacuous calls to collections methods. The method list.containsAll(list) will always return true because a collection always contains all its own elements. The method list.retainAll(list) has no effect because it retains all elements of the collection that are also in the collection itself, which is all of them.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method, which contains vacuous calls to collections methods. The testShowBugContainsAll method expects the result of showBug to be false, but since showBug always returns true due to the vacuous call to containsAll, the test fails. The testShowBugRetainAll method indirectly triggers the bug by calling showBug, and the assertion fails because showBug always returns true.
